text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high 5xx rate on /api/v1/generate in us-west-2 — 5m error-rate 21%, p95 latency 2.1s, spike started ~18:03 UTC
sre-jordan: ack — oncall. checking dashboards and recent deploys. status on infra changes? :mag:
maya-cs: customer CUST-3321 reported widget timeouts at ~18:05 UTC, multiple retries logged on their side.
ingrid-eng-platform: no CI deploys in last 3h. we did flip max_batch_size yesterday morning to 64 to squeeze throughput.
kate-eng-runtime: looking at batcher telemetry: aggregate queue_depth went from ~10 to 240 in 4m. batch composition skewed — large token requests clustered. HOL blocking suspected. pulling samples now.
hailey-eng-sre: ingress showing intermittent 502/504s. backend target groups appear healthy though. connection_count per worker up.
sre-jordan: paste a couple of batch samples and any errors you see. want to confirm if small requests are stuck behind long ones.
kate-eng-runtime: sample logs (snips):
```
batcher: enqueue id=req_71 size_tokens=8192 model=vicuna-13b
batcher: enqueue id=req_72 size_tokens=32 model=vicuna-13b
scheduler: created batch=243 members=[req_71,req_72] est_exec=3.8s
runtime: token-gen delayed, deadline miss for id=req_72
gateway: 504 backend read timeout for id=req_72
```
hailey-eng-sre: yep classic head-of-line — one huge request sitting at head of worker batch. p99 queue depth and p99 wait time skyrocketed.
sre-jordan: immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk first): 1) enable preemptive scheduling (so short tasks can be pulled ahead), 2) reduce max_batch_size to 16, 3) temporarily route non-critical endpoints (/embed) to vicuna-7b warm pool, 4) set drop_on_overflow=true for tiny tasks. who can apply?
kate-eng-runtime: I can toggle batcher flags; some are dynamic via configmap reload. prepping the patch.
hailey-eng-sre: I can open a temporary route to route /embed to fallback 7b pool for 30min. creating change right now.
ingrid-eng-platform: note: changing max_batch_size was done to improve throughput earlier; reverting will lower throughput but improve tail latency. agree with mitigations.

kate-eng-runtime: applying config changes: patching batcher configmap:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap batcher-config --patch '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"16","enable_preemption":"true","drop_on_overflow":"true"}}'
```
deploy-bot: configmap patched by kate-eng-runtime — reload triggered (reload-id: reload-9032)
hailey-eng-sre: routing PR merged to route /embed to vicuna-7b warm pool. propagation in progress.

sre-jordan: monitor metrics — check error-rate and queue_depth 60s after changes.
kate-eng-runtime: +60s: error-rate dropped to ~7%, p95 latency ~0.9s, median queue_depth ~20. good initial improvement.
ingrid-eng-platform: still seeing rare 504s (~0.6%). some workers still finishing long-running requests; consider bumping ingress backend timeout to 60s temporarily.
hailey-eng-sre: ingress timeout increased to 60s for vicuna services — applied.
sre-jordan: scaling option: add 3 extra batcher replicas in us-west-2 to spread load. initiating scale-up; node pool has capacity.
kate-eng-runtime: scale-up started, new pods scheduling.
maya-cs: CS update: informing CUST-3321 and CUST-3344 that we observed intermittent timeouts and are applying mitigations; asking them to retry in ~10 minutes.
sre-jordan: plan for handoff: if error-rate <3% for 10m and queue_depth stable, I'll transition to monitoring and hand to kate-eng-runtime for root-cause. @kate-eng-runtime please take post-incident ownership.
kate-eng-runtime: taking owner. repro testing preemption behavior now. found scheduler issue: with preemption off we used arrival-order batching; with max_batch_size=64 a single giant request could monopolize batch execution. also no size-aware splitting.
hailey-eng-sre: can we surface a short-term guard to prevent worst-case blocking? e.g., soft limit default max_tokens=4096 with advisory or return 413 for >8192 until we implement splitting.
maya-cs: customers running legitimate large jobs prefer soft-fail with advisory and an opt-in for larger tokens via support. CS recommends opt-in flag rather than hard 413 by default.
kate-eng-runtime: short-term approach: enforce soft advisory at gateway for >4096 and reject >16384 with 413. long-term: implement size-aware batching that splits huge requests or time-slices them to avoid HOL.
sre-jordan: open incident ticket and runbook items.
hailey-eng-sre: INC-2002 created and linked to this thread. assigning: kate-eng-runtime (scheduler fix), hailey-eng-sre (runbook+timeouts), maya-cs (customer comms), ingrid-eng-platform (default batch sizing).
kate-eng-runtime: will open PR for size-aware batching and per-request token telemetry within 24h. will also add batch composition metrics to dashboards.
maya-cs: CS will prepare a proactive message to top affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fix.
sre-jordan: monitoring window: error-rate now at 1.5% sustained for 20m, queue_depth normalized across nodes. closing active pages, moving incident to MONITORING. if metrics regress, page eng-runtime.
incident-bot: Incident state -> MONITORING by <@sre-jordan>. incident id INC-2002. acknowledged participants: <@kate-eng-runtime>, <@hailey-eng-sre>, <@ingrid-eng-platform>, <@maya-cs>
sre-jordan: thanks team. postmortem scheduled in #postmortems on 2026-03-16 21:00 UTC. we will include timeline, mitigation steps, and customer impact summary.
